newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended slightly down on Wednesday following losses on Tuesday on continuing profit-taking from retail investors, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,327 yuan ($401) per tonne, losing one yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,330 and a low of 3,320.
The March, May and July contracts did not trade, November fell six to 3,332 and the January 1998 contract was down six to 3,340.
Combined volume rose to 25,000 tonnes from 23,300.

Soybeans opened up slightly but profit-taking pushed prices down for most of the session with many investors staying on the sidelines following the technical corrections of the past two days, traders said.
"Profit-taking was the major factor for the day's falls, but there was strong support at low levels with fundamentals improved," one trader said.
"Most investors took a wait-and-see attitude," he added.
Traders said fundamentals had improved and soybeans were likely to rebound after a few days.
